To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relationships between solar flares with the sunspot activity and the geomagnetic activity are well described by an integrative response model with the time scale of about 8 months for the former and 13 months for the latter.
the relationships between solar flares with sunspot and geomagentic activity can be well described using an integral response model.

the relationships between the solar flare parameters and sunspot activity as well as those of geomagnetic activity to solar flares are well described by an integrative response model with the decay time scales of about one year.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships among the flare parameters and the geomagnetic and sunspot activities.
the relationship between solar flare parameters and geomagnetic activity (the aa index).

the following: (1) the relationship between solar flares and geomagnetic activity (AA index) and sunspot number (RZ) in a solar cycle; (2) the prediction of time delay of the flare index with respect to RZ and AA index; (3) the prediction of the peak time of the flare index in a solar cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solar flare is an indicator of the solar magnetic activity and that the geomagnetic activity is an indicator of solar flare activity.

solar flares have been found to be closely associated with sunspot activity and geomagnetic activity, and they are related to the accumulated solar magnetic activity in the past through time decay factors.
there exists a strong relationship between solar flares and sunspots, but the relationship between solar flaras and geomagnetic activity is weak.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solar flare is a kind of solar magnetic activity and the geomagnetic activity may be caused by both solar flare and sunspot.
solar flares, sunspot activity, and geomagnetic activity have the same origin.
the solar flares are a kind of geomagnetic activity, which is related to the sunspot activity.

solar flares can be predicted in a solar cycle by using the geomagnetic activity index (aa index).
solar flares have a long-term memory.
solar flares may be a response to sunspot activity with a time delay.
